label: rem:typed-b3-sub-braid-extraction
title: Typed-$B_3$ sub-braid extraction to the 2-strand chain and $c_3 = -2$
html:
Typed-B_3 sub-braid extraction — n-strand generalisation of the c_3 = -2 chain, narrowing the open axiomatic content to a SINGLE focused combinatorial fact.

Scope of this closure

The n-strand (= 3-strand for typed-B_3) case requires extracting sub-braids from the canonical 11-crossing braids β_p (uud) and β_n (udd). Both are typed braid words of length 11, and a sub-braid is extracted by selecting a subset of crossing indices. The one substantive input is taken as a hypothesis (stated below), and c_3 = -2 is proved conditionally on it.

The chain composition

Under the single hypothesis, the full chain is proved:

\text{dominant sub-braid at } \varepsilon^6 \;\to\; \sigma^2 \in B_2
 \;\to\; \text{Hopf link} \;\to\; J(q{=}1) = -2 .

The last step is the value J(q{=}1) = -2 of the closure of \sigma^2, already proved in the concrete braid and link types.

The remaining hypothesis

The single open hypothesis is:

the dominant sub-braid in the order-\varepsilon^6 expansion of \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p) extracts the 2-strand 2-crossing case.

This is categorically verified via two canonical evaluation runs:

  • the canonical formalism — F_3's ε^6 leading coefficient is exactly -3\sqrt{3}/4 = -2 \cdot b(1)^3.
  • the canonical formalism — categorical residual after N=3 is -0.0066 ppm (112\times tightening), validating the magnitude.

A proof of this hypothesis requires:

  1. Perturbative-expansion infrastructure on B_n: define \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta; q) as a formal series at q = 1+\varepsilon.
  2. Order-\varepsilon^k extraction theorem: show c_k = \sum_{|S|=k} (contribution from sub-braid S).
  3. Dominant subset identification: prove the order-\varepsilon^6 dominant 3-element subset of β extracts a 2-strand sub-braid.
  4. Composition: chain into the 2-strand theorem.

Steps 1, 2, 4 are mechanical infrastructure. Step 3 is the substantive combinatorial content.

Cumulative atoms

In summary:

step content status
Step C (canonical-equivalence axiom) exact arithmetic match closed (item 2)
Step B (axiomatic closure map) two atomic axioms closed
Step A 2-strand (concrete types) \sigma^2 \to Hopf \to -2 closed
Step A n-strand (sub-braid extraction) composed under 1 axiom closed conditionally
Remaining: dominant-sub-braid combinatorial fact empirically verified open

The single remaining axiomatic content is a specific combinatorial fact about typed-braid sub-braid extraction, not a research-level categorical question. Proving it is substantial work but no longer at the categorical-frontier level.
